text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher indicated in a German newspaper interview that there might be more attacks against Iraq if Saddam Hussein failed to understand the "message" of this week's missile strikes.

In an interview with Bild am Sonntag released ahead of publication on Sunday, Christopher was quoted as saying the cruise missile strikes against Iraq were an "appropriate response" to Iraq's incursion into the Kurdish north.
"We are satisfied with our necessary and appropriate response," Christopher told the newspaper. "It is the right message to Saddam Hussein."
Christopher added: "We very much hope that Saddam truly understands the message that we delivered. If he doesn't, we reserve the right to proceed with further appropriate steps."

U.S. cruise missiles severely damaged Iraqi air defences this week, destroying or damaging up to 11 of 15 targets, the Pentagon said on Friday, in its first public assessment of the raids on southern Iraq.

The satellite-guided missiles were fired from over 800 km (500 miles) away in two strikes against air defence targets in southern Iraq to punish Saddam for a military drive into a Western-protected "safe haven" for Kurds in northern Iraq.
